main_text.p: leritis.[?] Secuta est diuina νέμεσις[?], cùm magna rerum illius μεταβολὴ[?] & inclinatione facta, tandem à Siroë filio captus, numellis & compedibus constrictus, in carcere diu detentus, & à satrapis filij mandatu conspurus, & horribili genere supplicij, sagittis cõfixus, interijt. Dignum est memoratu Valerij Maximi dictum: Lento gradu ad sui uindictam diuina procedit ira, tarditatemq; supplicij grauitate pœ-næ compensat. Et exstat Plutarchi Com-mentarius de sera Numinis uindicta:

Iam uerò, quòd præmia rectè factorū attinet, cùm non ex merito, sed ex gratia conferantur, quis non uideat, nequaquam nobis ante tempus diuinitus præstitutū esse exigenda? Ergo cùm citò conferun-tur, gratiæ Deo, sua dona coronanti, agē-dæ: cùm differuntur, æquis animis exspe standa sunt.

4. Ex ignorantia autem finium bonorum & malorum, nascitur opinio negās, ex malis ἀγνωσίαν[?] quandam ad nos redire. Quid boni secuturum esset ex scelere Patriarcharum fratrem Iosephū uendentium, nemo hominum potuit conijcere. Et tamen Deus id Iosepho mirabili qua-

page.notes: The signature mark at the lower left of the page (a small symbol near the catchword) is not clearly readable and is left out. Greek words are copied as far as they can be read: νέμεσις, μεταβολὴ and ἀγνωσίαν are doubtful in their accents and letters. The first word "leritis" is uncertain in its initial letter. The line "Et tamen" is set with tight spacing; read as "Et tamen".
